svg.aria-label: LegacyScan output for a generated Spring Security configuration on Spring Boot 4.1: 7 findings, 6 of them APIs that were removed
svg.text: examples/legacy-shop
src/main/java/com/example/shop/SecurityConfig.java
9 removed Declare a SecurityFilterChain bean instead of extending WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter
[security-filter-chain] (+1 more in this file)
WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter was deprecated in Spring Security 5.7 and removed in 6.0 (Spring
Boot 3). Security configuration is now a set of beans.
16 deprecated Use @EnableMethodSecurity instead of @EnableGlobalMethodSecurity [enable-method-security]
@EnableGlobalMethodSecurity is deprecated in Spring Security 6. @EnableMethodSecurity turns on
@PreAuthorize and @PostAuthorize by default, so prePostEnabled = true is no longer needed.
24 removed Configure HttpSecurity with the lambda DSL, without and() [security-lambda-dsl]
The chained style, csrf().disable() joined with and(), was deprecated in Spring Security 6.1 and
removed in 7.0 (Spring Boot 4). Each configurer takes a lambda, available since 5.2.
25 removed Configure HttpSecurity with the lambda DSL, without and() [security-lambda-dsl]
26 removed Configure HttpSecurity with the lambda DSL, without and() [security-lambda-dsl]
27 removed Use authorizeHttpRequests instead of authorizeRequests [authorize-http-requests]
authorizeRequests() was deprecated in Spring Security 6 and removed in 7.0 (Spring Boot 4).
authorizeHttpRequests() is its replacement, built on the AuthorizationManager API.
28 removed Use requestMatchers instead of antMatchers, mvcMatchers and regexMatchers [request-matchers]
antMatchers(), mvcMatchers() and regexMatchers() were deprecated in Spring Security 5.8 and
removed in 6.0 (Spring Boot 3). requestMatchers() picks the right matcher for the application.
Project: Java 21, Spring Boot 4.1 [pom.xml]
7 findings in 1 of 1 file: 6 removed, 1 deprecated
Carbon date: 2019. The oldest pattern here (security-lambda-dsl) has had a standard replacement for 7 years.
Read a guide: java LegacyScan.java explain <id>
